roots.description: Two root paths to synchronize. First is local (or remote via `ssh://`), second is the partner (local or remote). For remote, use `ssh://user@host/path` format.

items.description: Root path (local path or remote URI)

log.description: Enable logging of synchronization actions to console.

logfile.description: Path to a log file. If empty, no file logging is done.

verbose.description: Verbosity level: 0 (quiet) to 4 (detailed debug). Higher values show more info about each step.

prefer.description: Which side to prefer when a conflict occurs (newer file wins). Other options: older, error, never.

copier.description: Conflict resolution strategy. 'newer' (default): copy file from side with newer timestamp. 'error' stops on conflicts.

fastcheck.description: Use fast MD5-based checksums for large files to reduce network transfer during comparison.

follow.description: Whether to follow symbolic links. Valid: 'true', 'false', 'both'.

sshcmd.description: Command to use for SSH connections. You can specify custom options (e.g., 'ssh -p 2222 -i /id_ed25519').

port.description: SSH port to use when connecting to remote hosts. Set to 0 to use default SSH port (22).

excludes.description: List of paths (relative to roots) to exclude entirely from synchronization.

includes.description: Optional list of paths to explicitly include — useful when an earlier `ignore` directive would have excluded them.

ignorepatterns.description: List of filename patterns (regex-compatible) to ignore in all directories.

perms.description: Preserve file permissions and ownership (requires proper filesystem support and privileges).

batch.description: Run in non-interactive mode — abort on any prompt requiring user input. Useful for cron jobs.

retry.description: Number of times to retry connection on network failure before aborting.

times.description: Preserve modification times (timestamps) of files during sync.

delete.description: Whether to delete files that exist on only one side. Options: 'yes', 'no', 'nonroot' (default for bidirectional — deletes only from non-root roots, i.e., from the secondary side).
